Before Day 1

A cycle, not an invented deadline

This is a scalable 84-day cycle, not a claim that your exam is 12 weeks away. No exam date, available study hours or current ability is assumed. Begin with the diagnostic and adapt to the actual notification/calendar and your accuracy. The default plan gives 90–95% priority to prelims; tiny mains-overlap exercises are optional and limited.

01

Keep a small source stack

One history reference, one polity reference, one Hindi book, one UP GK book and one solved PYQ compilation if needed. NCERT is a foundation/repair resource, not a demand to read classes 6–12 in full. Paid books are optional; links go to lawful catalogues, never pirated copies.

02

Attempt, explain, revisit

Practise text-based PYQ adaptations inside each day. Answers and explanations stay hidden until you reveal them. Source scans are secondary, because marked choices spoil practice. Revisit after 1, 7 and 21 days. A repeated question is retrieval practice, not fresh-mock proof.

03

Make the pace realistic

If you miss a day, resume the unfinished work; do not double tomorrow's load. Use revision days for a small backlog. At 2 hours/day, reduce first-pass reading and extend the cycle. Actual 3-hour simulations need a longer block, or an honestly labelled split attempt.

Ordinary-day time budget (minutes)
Block4 hours2 hoursKeep this outcome
GS9040One named topic, one map/table/summary
Hindi4525One rule/category, a small example set
PYQs + explanation4525Fewer questions if needed; never remove explanation review
Current affairs + UP3015Five dated facts at most, with static connections
Recall + errors3015Delayed retrieval and the next repair task

Full-paper days are different: 180 minutes for GS + Hindi together, then 60 minutes of triage. Detailed repair starts the next day. At 2 hours/day, split over two days and move the schedule forward; do not compress 3 hours into 2.

Syllabus source check · 22 November 2026

Use the revised 2026 scheme

Basis: advertisement A-4/E-1/2026 dated 26 October 2026; Appendix 2 and 3, PDF pages 7–8. The official UPPSC notification listing (opens a new tab) identifies the advertisement. The full eight-page document used here is a Prepp-hosted notification mirror (opens a new tab), not an UPPSC-hosted PDF. Official advertisement deep links can require a session; open UPPSC home → Notifications → the matching advertisement and confirm any later corrigendum.

Some “2026 syllabus” pages still show two prelims papers and an old 400-mark mains. Do not use those summaries as the current scheme. A vacancy-bifurcation PDF is not the full syllabus. This website is study guidance, not application/eligibility advice.

Prelims: one objective paper

200 questions / 200 marks / 3 hours: 140 GS and 60 Hindi. Wrong/multiple-marked answers receive the notified one-third penalty; unanswered questions have no penalty. Use the instructions printed for your actual exam.

GS scope: general science; Indian history and national movement; polity, economy and culture; agriculture, commerce and trade; population, ecology and urbanisation; world/Indian geography and natural resources; current national/international events; general intelligence; special UP knowledge of education, culture, agriculture, industry, trade, living and social traditions.

हिन्दी: छह क्षेत्र, हर क्षेत्र 10 प्रश्न

विलोम शब्द; वाक्य/वर्तनी का अशुद्धि-शोधन; वाक्यांश के लिए एक शब्द; तत्सम–तद्भव; विशेष्य–विशेषण; पर्यायवाची।

रोज छोटा अभ्यास करें। सामान्य दिखने वाला शब्द भी अर्थ या प्रयोग में भ्रमित कर सकता है। पिछले प्रश्नों में नियम पहचानें, केवल चिह्नित विकल्प न याद करें। सामान्य अध्ययन अंग्रेज़ी या हिन्दी में पढ़ सकते हैं, पर हिन्दी का अभ्यास हिन्दी में ही करें।

नीचे छहों क्षेत्रों के वास्तविक प्रश्न-संदर्भ जुड़े हैं; नई सूचियों से पहले अपनी पुरानी त्रुटियाँ ठीक करें।

Mains: four descriptive papers, each 200 marks / 3 hours, total 800: GS I, GS II, General Hindi and Drafting, Hindi Essay. This cycle postpones dedicated mains work until prelims is secure. See the later roadmap.

01Foundation · Diagnostic Diagnostic, not a judgement0/5

Full-paper day: 3 h attempt + 1 h triage. With only 2 h/day, spread this over two days and shift the cycle; a split attempt is not a 3 h simulation.

Attempt the 2021 GS and Hindi papers together without looking at solutions. Set a 180-minute timer and use a numbered answer sheet. If 3 uninterrupted hours are not available, split the attempt into two sessions and label it untimed/split, not exam simulation.

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q53 · PDF p12

In which part of the Constitution are the provisions on elections grouped?

Answer: C. Part XV

Part XV covers elections, including the Election Commission framework. Fundamental Rights are in Part III; emergency provisions are in Part XVIII.

Editorial explanation, not an official key. Constitution of India (opens a new tab)

Articles 23 and 24 primarily protect which fundamental right?

Article 23 prohibits trafficking and forced labour; Article 24 concerns child employment in specified hazardous settings. Articles 19–22 concern freedoms/protections, not this pair.

Which constitutional institution recommends how specified tax proceeds should be shared between the Union and states?

The Finance Commission's Article 280 role includes recommendations on distribution of net tax proceeds and grants. It recommends; it does not itself legislate the tax.

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q23 · PDF p5

Who was the first woman to preside over the Indian National Congress, distinct from its first Indian woman president?

Answer: C. Annie Besant

Annie Besant presided in 1917. Sarojini Naidu, in 1925, was the first Indian woman president. This distinction is the trap, not simply recognition of a famous name.

03Foundation · Polity Fundamental Rights: structure and scope0/5

Standard day: 4 h total. For 2 h, use 40 / 25 / 25 / 15 / 15 minutes; halve the reading/examples, keep explanation review, and extend the cycle where necessary.

Read NCERT Rights in the Indian Constitution and Articles 12–35 selectively. Separate equality, freedom, exploitation, religion, cultural/educational rights and remedies. Compare rights of citizens with rights of all persons.

Produce: A rights–article–beneficiary table. Explain Articles 15 and 16 without confusing their grounds or purpose.

Read from: NCERT textbooks: official free portal (opens a new tab) · M. Laxmikanth: Indian Polity (opens a new tab) · Constitution of India (opens a new tab). Use the named topic/chapter, not the entire book. Free alternatives and book-selection guidance.

पर्यायवाची: 10 मूल शब्दों के अर्थ-समूह बनाएं; हर समूह में एक असमानार्थक शब्द अलग करें। सप्ताह 1–4 में छोटे अर्थ-समूह और नियम बनाएं, विशाल सूची नहीं। नीचे हिन्दी के प्रश्न-कार्डों पर पहले स्वयं उत्तर दें, फिर उत्तर दिखाएँ।

Articles 23 and 24 primarily protect which fundamental right?

Answer: D. Protection against exploitation

Article 23 prohibits trafficking and forced labour; Article 24 concerns child employment in specified hazardous settings. Articles 19–22 concern freedoms/protections, not this pair.

‘कुछ लोग आए’ में ‘कुछ’ का विशेषण-भेद क्या है?

उत्तर: A. अनिश्चित संख्यावाचक

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q28 · PDF p6

A is seventh from the left, B fourth from the right. After swapping, A is fifteenth from the left. What is B's new position from the right?

Answer: C. Twelfth

B's original left position was 15, so total = 15 + 4 − 1 = 18. B moves to left position 7; from the right it is 18 − 7 + 1 = 12.

A person leaves at 6:40 AM, travels for 25 minutes, then spends 15 minutes at breakfast. When does the next journey start?

Answer: B. 7:20 AM

6:40 + 25 minutes = 7:05; another 15 minutes gives 7:20. Time for the later journey does not enter the departure time asked.

08Foundation · Polity Union executive0/5

Standard day: 4 h total. For 2 h, use 40 / 25 / 25 / 15 / 15 minutes; halve the reading/examples, keep explanation review, and extend the cycle where necessary.

Read President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers. Distinguish election, appointment, tenure, constitutional role and actual executive responsibility.

Produce: A four-office comparison; draw the chain of collective responsibility to Lok Sabha.

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q54 · PDF p12

Identify the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

Answer: A. G. V. Mavalankar

G. V. Mavalankar became the first Lok Sabha Speaker in 1952. The other names belong to later periods.

Editorial explanation, not an official key. M. Laxmikanth: Indian Polity (opens a new tab)

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q55 · PDF p12

Articles 23 and 24 primarily protect which fundamental right?

Answer: D. Protection against exploitation

Article 23 prohibits trafficking and forced labour; Article 24 concerns child employment in specified hazardous settings. Articles 19–22 concern freedoms/protections, not this pair.

Editorial explanation, not an official key. Constitution of India (opens a new tab)

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q115 · PDF p24

Which constitutional institution recommends how specified tax proceeds should be shared between the Union and states?

Answer: B. Finance Commission

The Finance Commission's Article 280 role includes recommendations on distribution of net tax proceeds and grants. It recommends; it does not itself legislate the tax.

Editorial explanation, not an official key. Constitution of India (opens a new tab)

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q116 · PDF p24

The description 'quasi-federal' for India's constitutional system is associated with which scholar?

Answer: A. K. C. Wheare

K. C. Wheare used this description to emphasise the strong central features alongside federal arrangements. Do not confuse this attribution with a constitutional article.

Editorial explanation, not an official key. M. Laxmikanth: Indian Polity (opens a new tab)

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q52 · PDF p12

Which constitutional provision specifically prohibits discrimination on listed grounds in public employment?

Answer: B. Article 16(2)

Article 16 concerns equality of opportunity in public employment. Clause (2) lists prohibited grounds; Article 15 concerns a different general discrimination provision.

Editorial explanation, not an official key. Constitution of India (opens a new tab)

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q53 · PDF p12

In which part of the Constitution are the provisions on elections grouped?

Answer: C. Part XV

Part XV covers elections, including the Election Commission framework. Fundamental Rights are in Part III; emergency provisions are in Part XVIII.

Editorial explanation, not an official key. Constitution of India (opens a new tab)

मानक वर्तनी चुनें।

उत्तर: D. अधीन

मानक रूप ‘अधीन’ है। शब्द को उसकी सही मात्रा के साथ लिखकर पुनः स्मरण करें, केवल विकल्प-क्रम न याद करें।

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q143 · PDF p29

सर्वनाम-प्रयोग की दृष्टि से मानक रूप चुनें।

उत्तर: B. मुझे यह पसंद नहीं।

यहाँ कर्म/अनुभवकर्ता के लिए ‘मुझे’ मानक रूप है। ‘मेरे को’ बोलचाल में मिल सकता है, पर इस औपचारिक व्याकरण-अभ्यास में ‘मुझे’ चुनें। वाक्य मूल प्रश्न से सरल करके लिखा गया है।

Editorial explanation, not an official key. वासुदेवनन्दन प्रसाद: आधुनिक हिन्दी व्याकरण और रचना (opens a new tab)

‘सूक्ष्म’ के विपरीत अर्थ की सही जोड़ी कौन-सी है?

उत्तर: C. सूक्ष्म–स्थूल

सूक्ष्म का विलोम स्थूल है। अर्थ का आकार/बारीकी वाला पक्ष देखें; कोमल और लघु समान विलोम नहीं हैं।

अभिज्ञ का अर्थ जानकार/परिचित है; अनभिज्ञ का अर्थ जानकारी न रखने वाला है। सर्वज्ञ और विज्ञ विपरीत अर्थ नहीं देते।

Create an event–cause–leader–place chronology, not disconnected dates.

15Foundation · History British expansion and revenue0/5

Standard day: 4 h total. For 2 h, use 40 / 25 / 25 / 15 / 15 minutes; halve the reading/examples, keep explanation review, and extend the cycle where necessary.

Study expansion, Subsidiary Alliance, Doctrine of Lapse and Permanent/Ryotwari/Mahalwari settlements. Link revenue systems to location and effect on peasants.

Produce: A policy–administrator–region–impact table and six chronological anchors.

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q119 · PDF p25

Which Congress session adopted the Purna Swaraj goal in 1929?

Answer: D. Lahore

The Lahore session of December 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, adopted Purna Swaraj. The independence observance followed on 26 January 1930.

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q124 · PDF p26

Permanent Settlement is most directly associated with which region?

Answer: C. Bengal

Permanent Settlement was introduced in Bengal in 1793. Ryotwari is associated with major parts of Madras/Bombay; Mahalwari with parts of northern India.

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q23 · PDF p5

Who was the first woman to preside over the Indian National Congress, distinct from its first Indian woman president?

Answer: C. Annie Besant

Annie Besant presided in 1917. Sarojini Naidu, in 1925, was the first Indian woman president. This distinction is the trap, not simply recognition of a famous name.

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q90 · PDF p19

Which of these places was annexed under Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse?

Answer: A. Jhansi

Jhansi was a Doctrine of Lapse annexation. Punjab and Awadh were acquired through different grounds/events; do not classify every British annexation as lapse.

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q143 · PDF p29

सर्वनाम-प्रयोग की दृष्टि से मानक रूप चुनें।

उत्तर: B. मुझे यह पसंद नहीं।

यहाँ कर्म/अनुभवकर्ता के लिए ‘मुझे’ मानक रूप है। ‘मेरे को’ बोलचाल में मिल सकता है, पर इस औपचारिक व्याकरण-अभ्यास में ‘मुझे’ चुनें। वाक्य मूल प्रश्न से सरल करके लिखा गया है।

Choose the correct sequence from earliest to latest.

Who was the first woman to preside over the Indian National Congress, distinct from its first Indian woman president?

Answer: C. Annie Besant

Annie Besant presided in 1917. Sarojini Naidu, in 1925, was the first Indian woman president. This distinction is the trap, not simply recognition of a famous name.

‘कुछ लोग आए’ में ‘कुछ’ का विशेषण-भेद क्या है?

उत्तर: A. अनिश्चित संख्यावाचक

‘लोग’ गिने जा सकते हैं लेकिन संख्या निश्चित नहीं है, इसलिए ‘कुछ’ अनिश्चित संख्यावाचक है। ‘कुछ पानी’ में मात्रा होने से परिमाण का प्रसंग अलग होगा। स्कैन का हाथ से चिह्नित विकल्प इस नियम का प्रमाण नहीं है।

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q152 · PDF p30

‘कुछ लोग आए’ में ‘कुछ’ का विशेषण-भेद क्या है?

उत्तर: A. अनिश्चित संख्यावाचक

‘लोग’ गिने जा सकते हैं लेकिन संख्या निश्चित नहीं है, इसलिए ‘कुछ’ अनिश्चित संख्यावाचक है। ‘कुछ पानी’ में मात्रा होने से परिमाण का प्रसंग अलग होगा। स्कैन का हाथ से चिह्नित विकल्प इस नियम का प्रमाण नहीं है।

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q103 · PDF p22

General yellowing with poor plant growth commonly indicates deficiency of which major nutrient?

Answer: D. Nitrogen

Nitrogen deficiency commonly causes pale/yellow leaves and reduced growth. Symptom pattern and leaf age matter in real diagnosis; this is the general exam-level association.

Photosynthesis chiefly converts light energy into which stored form?

Answer: A. Chemical energy in organic food

Plants use light energy to form organic compounds, storing chemical energy. Sugar may later be converted into starch; that conversion does not itself explain every step of light-energy capture.

‘कुछ लोग आए’ में ‘कुछ’ का विशेषण-भेद क्या है?

उत्तर: A. अनिश्चित संख्यावाचक

‘लोग’ गिने जा सकते हैं लेकिन संख्या निश्चित नहीं है, इसलिए ‘कुछ’ अनिश्चित संख्यावाचक है। ‘कुछ पानी’ में मात्रा होने से परिमाण का प्रसंग अलग होगा। स्कैन का हाथ से चिह्नित विकल्प इस नियम का प्रमाण नहीं है।

Editorial explanation, not an official key. Independent reference (opens a new tab)

उत्तर: A. अनिश्चित संख्यावाचक

किसी बात की इच्छा/आकांक्षा से रहित व्यक्ति के लिए उपयुक्त शब्द क्या है?

उत्तर: B. निःस्पृह

निःस्पृह का अर्थ इच्छा/स्पृहा से रहित है। निर्भीक भय का अभाव बताता है, जिज्ञासु जानने की इच्छा रखता है।

Answer: D. Urban areas are warmer than nearby rural areas

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q28 · PDF p6

A is seventh from the left, B fourth from the right. After swapping, A is fifteenth from the left. What is B's new position from the right?

Answer: C. Twelfth

B's original left position was 15, so total = 15 + 4 − 1 = 18. B moves to left position 7; from the right it is 18 − 7 + 1 = 12.

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q57 · PDF p13

A person leaves at 6:40 AM, travels for 25 minutes, then spends 15 minutes at breakfast. When does the next journey start?

Answer: B. 7:20 AM

6:40 + 25 minutes = 7:05; another 15 minutes gives 7:20. Time for the later journey does not enter the departure time asked.

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q26 · PDF p6

A bag has ₹5, ₹2 and ₹1 coins in a 3:4:5 count ratio, worth ₹2,100 in total. How many ₹5 coins are there?

Answer: D. 225

Let counts be 3x, 4x and 5x. Value is 15x + 8x + 5x = 28x = 2100, so x = 75 and the ₹5-coin count is 225. Do not confuse value ratio with count ratio.

A bag has ₹5, ₹2 and ₹1 coins in a 3:4:5 count ratio, worth ₹2,100 in total. How many ₹5 coins are there?

Answer: D. 225

Let counts be 3x, 4x and 5x. Value is 15x + 8x + 5x = 28x = 2100, so x = 75 and the ₹5-coin count is 225. Do not confuse value ratio with count ratio.

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q28 · PDF p6

A is seventh from the left, B fourth from the right. After swapping, A is fifteenth from the left. What is B's new position from the right?

Answer: C. Twelfth

B's original left position was 15, so total = 15 + 4 − 1 = 18. B moves to left position 7; from the right it is 18 − 7 + 1 = 12.

The Finance Commission's Article 280 role includes recommendations on distribution of net tax proceeds and grants. It recommends; it does not itself legislate the tax.

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q28 · PDF p6

A is seventh from the left, B fourth from the right. After swapping, A is fifteenth from the left. What is B's new position from the right?

Answer: C. Twelfth

B's original left position was 15, so total = 15 + 4 − 1 = 18. B moves to left position 7; from the right it is 18 − 7 + 1 = 12.

An urban heat island means what?

Answer: D. Urban areas are warmer than nearby rural areas

Built surfaces, less vegetation and waste heat can raise urban temperatures relative to nearby rural surroundings. This is a relative-temperature effect, not a claim that every city is always hotter.

Which constitutional institution recommends how specified tax proceeds should be shared between the Union and states?

The Finance Commission's Article 280 role includes recommendations on distribution of net tax proceeds and grants. It recommends; it does not itself legislate the tax.

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q26 · PDF p6

A bag has ₹5, ₹2 and ₹1 coins in a 3:4:5 count ratio, worth ₹2,100 in total. How many ₹5 coins are there?

Answer: D. 225

Let counts be 3x, 4x and 5x. Value is 15x + 8x + 5x = 28x = 2100, so x = 75 and the ₹5-coin count is 225. Do not confuse value ratio with count ratio.

Adapted PYQ · 2025 · Q28 · PDF p6

A is seventh from the left, B fourth from the right. After swapping, A is fifteenth from the left. What is B's new position from the right?

Answer: C. Twelfth

B's original left position was 15, so total = 15 + 4 − 1 = 18. B moves to left position 7; from the right it is 18 − 7 + 1 = 12.

A bag has ₹5, ₹2 and ₹1 coins in a 3:4:5 count ratio, worth ₹2,100 in total. How many ₹5 coins are there?

Answer: D. 225

Let counts be 3x, 4x and 5x. Value is 15x + 8x + 5x = 28x = 2100, so x = 75 and the ₹5-coin count is 225. Do not confuse value ratio with count ratio.

Schedule the next rolling current-affairs update and delayed error reviews. Keep the year asked in the paper. Use PIB: national developments and schemes (opens a new tab) · Drishti: UP monthly current-affairs archive (opens a new tab) only to verify relevant developments, not to silently replace the historical answer.

Revisit Day 83, Day 77, Day 63 notes/errors: one-day, seven-day and twenty-one-day recall where available. Log attempted/correct/wrong/blanks/unresolved separately for GS and Hindi. Use the review protocol; add follow-up dates, not just a score.

Cycle complete: review next steps below

Week-end check: Have compact revision sheets, a manageable error queue and a realistic next-cycle plan. If recall is weak, repeat the smallest relevant block before adding new material.

The work after an answer

Review errors, not just scores

Before checking

Write paper/file, question, your answer and confidence: known / reasoned / guessed / blank. Use a plain numbered answer sheet; do not peek at an annotated PDF's markings. Cover selections if possible. Already visible answers make the attempt a learning drill, not an unbiased diagnostic.

When reviewing

Classify each error: concept, memory, question-reading, elimination/guessing or time. Write the correct rule and why each distractor fails. Use an authenticated official final key when available; this site does not provide one. A handwritten/coaching answer is not official. Verify with a trustworthy text/primary source; leave genuinely disputed questions unresolved.

After a delay

Reattempt tomorrow, a week later and three weeks later. If the same rule fails twice, return to its short source section and make one comparison/diagram. Judge progress using accuracy and reduced repeat errors, not number of pages read or an invented “safe” score.

Copy this error-log structure into your own private notebook
Paper/file + QTopic + confidenceError causeRule + sourceReview queue
Exact linked file and numbere.g. fundamental rights; guessedConfused two provisionsWrite the distinction and source location+1 / +7 / +21 days; resolved or still uncertain

Mocks: Weeks 5–8 have one full-paper session/week; Weeks 9–12 have two. Most later sessions are explicitly labelled retests of a limited lawful paper library. They measure retrieval and pacing, not fresh-paper readiness. Add an unseen, current 200-question / 180-minute mock from a lawful source you already use; check its syllabus and replace a scheduled retest rather than adding extra hours. No unverified commercial mock is recommended here.

Practice score calculator

Enter counts after resolving answers. Uses C − W/3; blanks have no penalty. This is a study estimate, not UPPSC's result or a cutoff prediction. Keep unresolved/disputed answers out and label any partial score.

Paper-taking discipline: read the full stem, especially “not” and statement combinations; use two passes where helpful; reserve time for answer-sheet checking. Adjust GS/Hindi time from your practice evidence—there is no guaranteed attempt count. Multiple answers are penalised. Do not guess blindly to hit a target.

After Day 84: if the exam is still distant, keep one full paper/week plus repair, rolling CA and your weakest-topic cycle. If it is close, use the official date to taper new reading and prioritise recall/rest. If foundations remain weak, extend those weeks instead of pretending the entire syllabus is mastered.

Why question numbers differ between websites

Question order may differ between booklet series, reordered scans and mirrors. We found even files labelled UNHSIV-01 with different order. The daily links bind to the exact 34-page CareerPower PDF, not just a year/booklet label. Match the question topic as well as the number. PDF page numbers here count from the first page; they are not a guess about another scan.

What is verified, and what remains uncertain?

The current advertisement listing and full mirrored notification were inspected; the 2025 primary practice file's question numbers/pages were read, with Hindi pages visually checked. Paper/resource links were checked during publication. Third-party scans may contain annotations or OCR mistakes. Stable official full-advertisement and final-key download links were not established; no disputed answers or unverified topic weights are supplied. Recheck live portals for changes after 22 November 2026.

Selective reading, not an endless book list

Study materials and how to use them

Start free: NCERT, official Constitution, budgets, Census, PIB, state portals and the linked papers. If you own Laxmikanth, Spectrum or a Hindi/UP GK book, use that edition selectively. Commercial catalogue links are optional purchases, not free PDFs. Existing Lucent GK can help revise science/ancient/medieval facts, but it is not necessary; use NCERT here rather than an unverified download or seller. Do not buy every item below.

Official · free

NCERT textbooks: official free portal (opens a new tab)

Select class, subject and book, then the named chapter. Use Hindi or English for GS. Start with classes 6–10 only where foundations are weak; use class 11 Physical Geography / India: Physical Environment, class 12 India: People and Economy, class 11 Indian Economic Development and class 12 Introductory Macroeconomics selectively. New editions may rename chapters: match the topic, not a guessed page number. Do not read every book cover to cover.

Publisher catalogue · paid optional

M. Laxmikanth: Indian Polity (opens a new tab)

Read only the named topics for each day: Constitution, rights, institutions, federalism, bodies and local government. Your existing edition is adequate for static concepts; verify changes in law officially. Free alternative: NCERT political science plus the Constitution below. No paid course is necessary.

Official · free

Constitution of India (opens a new tab)

Use the current English or Hindi text to verify articles, rights and schedules. Read the relevant provision after attempting a polity question; do not try to memorise the whole document.

Publisher catalogue · paid optional

Spectrum: A Brief History of Modern India (opens a new tab)

One reference for British expansion, reform, nationalism and movements. Read selected sections named in the plan. Free foundation: NCERT history, especially class 8 Our Pasts III / equivalent colonial-history chapters. Avoid a second modern-history reference.

Publisher catalogue · paid optional

वासुदेवनन्दन प्रसाद: आधुनिक हिन्दी व्याकरण और रचना (opens a new tab)

एक ही व्याकरण पुस्तक पर्याप्त है। विलोम, पर्यायवाची, तत्सम–तद्भव, विशेष्य–विशेषण, वाक्यांश और अशुद्धि-शोधन वाले अंश पढ़ें। रोज नियम समझकर उदाहरण लिखें; पूरी पुस्तक एक साथ समाप्त करना लक्ष्य नहीं है। निःशुल्क शुरुआत: नीचे दिए वास्तविक हिन्दी प्रश्नपत्र और NCERT हिन्दी की पठनीय सामग्री; संदेह होने पर विश्वसनीय व्याकरण/शब्दकोश से पुष्टि करें।

Publisher catalogue · paid optional

Arihant: Uttar Pradesh GK / RO–ARO catalogue (opens a new tab)

Choose just one UP GK book (Hindi or English) and, if needed, one solved RO/ARO PYQ compilation. The catalogue also contains old-pattern practice sets: check the actual 200-question combined pattern before buying a mock. Use UP tourism, budget, Census and government sources below as free alternatives and updates.

Third-party study material · free archive

Drishti: UP monthly current-affairs archive (opens a new tab)

Choose one monthly compilation, not several coaching feeds. Read the latest completed month during daily sessions and work backwards through your backlog. Also cover national/international news through PIB. A rolling 6–12-month window is a planning starting point, not an official cutoff; adjust when the exam date is announced. Old paper current affairs are historical, not current facts.

Official · free

PIB: national developments and schemes (opens a new tab)

For selected developments, note what changed, ministry/institution, objective, eligibility, location and one static connection. Do not copy press releases or read every release.

Official · free

Union Budget and Economic Survey (opens a new tab)

Use the latest available Budget at a Glance / highlights and Survey chapter summaries. Understand deficit, spending, sectors and agriculture first. Date all numerical notes; do not memorise the entire Survey.

Official · free

Uttar Pradesh budget portal (opens a new tab)

Open the latest state budget documents. Record major schemes and sector priorities with year, units and source page in your own notebook. Separate actual expenditure, revised estimates and budget estimates.

Official · free

Reserve Bank of India (opens a new tab)

Verify monetary-policy terms and current rates from the latest policy statement. Focus on inflation, repo rate, CRR, banking and foreign-exchange basics; older PYQ values must keep their historical date.

Official · free

Census of India (opens a new tab)

Use the year explicitly asked in the paper (many questions use Census 2011). Compare density, literacy, sex ratio, urbanisation and growth; a percentage is not an absolute count. Verify the latest release status rather than assuming a later census dataset exists.

Official · free

UP Tourism: culture and places (opens a new tab)

Build district–place–river–tradition associations for UP. Focus on cultural circuits, heritage, religious sites and crafts; tourism descriptions are not a substitute for the whole history syllabus.

Official · free

Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (opens a new tab)

Use published statistics and scheme documents to verify crop seasons, production years, MSP and farmer support. Understand concepts before memorising rankings.

Official · free

NDMA: disaster-management resources (opens a new tab)

Read the relevant hazard guidance: flood, drought, earthquake and heat wave. Know mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery; link UP floods and Bundelkhand drought to geography.

Official · free

ISRO: missions and applications (opens a new tab)

Read mission overviews, launch-vehicle basics and remote-sensing applications. Note objective, agency and application, not engineering-level specifications.

Official · free

Rajbhasha: official Hindi dictionary resources (opens a new tab)

For the later mains Hindi roadmap, use official dictionary and administrative-language resources. Practise meanings in context and both translation directions; use the matching commercial-terminology section in your Hindi text as well. This portal is a terminology aid, not a complete mains textbook.

Later, not a distraction today

The mains bridge and post-prelims roadmap

During this prelims cycle, keep only one optional ≤30-minute/week overlap exercise inside revision: a 75-word original explanation or a five-line official-letter outline. Do not add daily essays, full descriptive tests or separate accounts preparation for RO General. Post-specific requirements belong to the official notification, not this general study routine.

Revised mains: 800 marks, four 3-hour descriptive papers
PaperStructurePreparation after prelims
GS I · 20010 × 8 marks / 75 words + 10 × 12 marks / 125 wordsHistory/art/culture, modern 1757–1947, post-independence to 1965, society, India/UP geography, environment/disasters, science/technology.
GS II · 200Same short/long answer structureConstitution/polity, governance, economy/agriculture, ethics/integrity and regional/national/international current affairs.
General Hindi and Drafting · 200Eight questions; some internal choiceComprehension/title/explanation/précis; tabular summary and official correspondence; administrative/commercial translation; idioms/proverbs; grammar/punctuation/correction; sounds, vocabulary/word formation and computer basics.
Hindi Essay · 200One essay from each section: 800 words / 80 marks; 1,200 words / 120 marksSection I: science/environment/technology, economy, agriculture/industry/trade, disasters. Section II: literature/culture, social/political issues, national/international events, development schemes/projects.

Stage 1 · Convert notes into answers

Use the actual time until mains, not an assumed fixed gap. Convert each prelims table into a short issue–evidence–conclusion note; add UP examples. Begin with one 75-word and one 125-word original answer/day, increasing only when content and structure improve. Cover society, post-independence and ethics gaps explicitly.

NCERT textbooks: official free portal (opens a new tab) · Constitution of India (opens a new tab) · NDMA: disaster-management resources (opens a new tab) · Union Budget and Economic Survey (opens a new tab)

Stage 2 · हिन्दी और आलेखन

गद्यांश का शीर्षक, व्याख्या और संक्षेपण; शासकीय/अर्द्धशासकीय पत्र, कार्यालय आदेश, परिपत्र, अनुस्मारक, ज्ञापन, विज्ञप्ति, टिप्पण और प्रतिवेदन का अभ्यास करें। अर्थ सुरक्षित रखें, अनावश्यक शब्द हटाएँ। प्रशासनिक व वाणिज्यिक शब्दावली का दोनों दिशाओं में अनुवाद और मुहावरे/लोकोक्तियों का वाक्य-प्रयोग करें।

वासुदेवनन्दन प्रसाद: आधुनिक हिन्दी व्याकरण और रचना (opens a new tab) · Rajbhasha: official Hindi dictionary resources (opens a new tab)

Stage 3 · Timed papers and essays

Plan essays before writing: thesis, dimensions, evidence/UP example, counterpoint and constructive conclusion. Practise the notified 800/1,200-word lengths. Gradually reach full 3-hour descriptive tests and review relevance, word limits, handwriting/legibility and completion. Older mains papers are style practice, not the revised 800-mark template.
